parsed.why: No trans-specific criminalisation or documented targeting, and a broad gender-identity discrimination statute and public LGBTIQ initiative are positive climate signals. Visitor-facing screening and facilities evidence is absent, so this is not risk-free.

The former gender-expression offence was struck down, but trans people had been targeted by police and official discrimination persisted afterward. Enforced same-sex-conduct laws and strict morality policing add substantial exposure, though post-ruling enforcement frequency is unclear.

Recent reporting documents serious anti-LGBT abuse, while trans-specific threats by legislators, hostile public attitudes, and weak or absent protection show meaningful hostility with thin recourse. No universal visitor-facing restriction or organized targeting is documented.

Same-sex conduct is decriminalized and a current national law provides enhanced protection for gender-identity-motivated violence. Enforcement and visitor-facing practices are undocumented; the protective statute is positive, but its operation is not established.

Hate-speech and hate-crime rules and some regional protections are positive, but enforcement is inconsistent, gender-identity safeguards are fragmented, and reported attacks have gone without effective police response. No universal visitor-facing restriction is documented.
